Joshua sent them out; and they went to set up the ambush, and stayed between Bethel and Ai on the west side of Ai; but Joshua stayed among the people that night.
He took about five thousand men, and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city.
There was not a man left in Ai or Bethel who didn’t go out after Israel. They left the city open, and pursued Israel.
the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;

The border passed along from there to Luz, to the side of Luz (also called Bethel), southward. The border went down to Ataroth Addar, by the mountain that lies on the south of Beth Horon the lower.

basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: The lead describes a modern Tabuk-region geographic region and notes scholarly proposals that “Midian” originally denoted a tribal confederation; Bible section discusses scriptural usages.
basisReference.assessmentJa: Relevant background, not proof of exact ancient borders or of a single stable geographic extent.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: 記事は地理的地域としてのMidianに加えて部族連合を論じ、地理的範囲も議論がある。22:4の elders は人々を指す用法であり、この記事だけで固定範囲を証明しない。

basisReference.sectionAndLines: § Ancient places named Migdol or Migdal, lines 134–142
basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: It describes the Exodus encampment between Migdol and the sea, then separate Egyptian Migdol/Magdalu proposals and archaeological sites.
basisReference.assessmentJa: The section is relevant but does not establish which ancient Migdol is the candidate in Numbers 33:7; profile must preserve that distinction.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: 「Ancient places named Migdol or Migdal」節は出エジプトの宿営地としてのMigdolに触れるが、民数記33:7の個別地点や現代位置は特定しない。

basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: Identifies the Edom-border mountain where Aaron died; Jebel Harun is customary identification while Jebel Madara is an alternative.
basisReference.assessmentJa: Correct place-section match, but the article documents competing proposed sites.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: 記事は聖書のホル山と伝統的な位置比定を扱っていますが、正確な所在地には議論があります。

basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: Separates a second Mount Hor in Numbers 34:7–8, identifies it as a northern land boundary, and reports traditional Nur/Amanus range identifications.
basisReference.assessmentJa: Correctly distinguishes the northern boundary feature from Edomite Mount Hor; traditional identification is not certain.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: 記事は北境のホル山をエドム側の同名山と区別し、所在地比定には諸説を示す。

basisReference.sectionAndLines: § Biblical / Extent of biblical Negev / Biblical reference, lines 441–452
basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: Says biblical “Negev” may refer to the northern semi-arid part of the modern Negev; mentions Numbers 13:17 and notes the term can also mean south.
basisReference.assessmentJa: Relevant semantic distinction; scope of the ancient region differs from the modern administrative/geographic region.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: 記事のBiblical節は聖書のNegebの範囲が現代ネゲブより北側に限られた可能性と、語の「南」という用法を記す。民数記13:17のSouthが地名か方位かは本文だけでは確定しない。

basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: Pisgah is rendered by some translators as a mountain name, often associated with Nebo; the article describes an east-Jordan cluster/region and records uncertain naming.
basisReference.assessmentJa: Relevant geographical background, not precise identification of every biblical Pisgah occurrence.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: 記事は聖書のPisgahを山頂または高地として扱い、ネボ山などとの関係を説明する。民数記21:20の地形語から単一の現代山頂を確定する根拠にはしない。

basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: Lists Rithmah at Numbers 33:18–19 and offers Wadi el-Rutmi as a possible location.
basisReference.assessmentJa: Textual station match; location is only a proposal.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: 一覧表はRithmahを旅程上の宿営地として挙げ、Wadi el-Rutmi説を紹介するが、位置は確定していない。

basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: Sebam redirects to Sibmah; the Sibmah entry calls Sebam a form used in one case and says the site is unknown.
basisReference.assessmentJa: The list supports an orthographic association, but the linked text does not independently establish that every occurrence denotes one place.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: 記事はセバムをシブマの異形と説明しています。聖書本文では異なる綴りが使われるため、同一の町と断定できる根拠にはなりません。

basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: Numbers 32:37–38 and Joshua 13:19 place it in Reuben; variants include Shibmah/Sebam/Shebam; site unknown.
basisReference.assessmentJa: Direct verse/name association; no modern point identification is supported.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: Sibmah節はNumbers 32:37–38のルベン領町とし、32:3のSebamを異形と説明する。所在地は不明。

basisReference.articleContentParaphraseJa: Lists Terah at Numbers 33:27–28 and offers two possible sites.
basisReference.assessmentJa: Textual station match; location is explicitly uncertain.

identityOrRelation.noteJa: 一覧表はTerahを旅程上の地名として挙げ、複数の現代位置候補を示す。

directNewReads.observedContentJa: The identification section distinguishes Ashtaroth (Tell Ashtara) from the wider Karnaim/Ashteroth Karnaim site debate; several candidate sites are reported.
directNewReads.identityOrRelationAssessment: The current note and modern-location field preserve the city/site distinction and uncertainty; no single archaeological location is asserted as certain.

directNewReads.observedContentJa: The current Amka article says Ringgren regards the modern name as preserving Beth Ha-Emek (Joshua 19:27), while Palmer gives a different etymology.
directNewReads.identityOrRelationAssessment: The profile uses this solely as a qualified name-continuity proposal; it explicitly avoids claiming that ancient and modern places are the same point.

directNewReads.observedContentJa: The article identifies Bethel as an ancient city, reports the common Beitin identification with alternatives, and its Joshua section states that Joshua 7:2 and 8:9 place Bethel west of Ai.
directNewReads.identityOrRelationAssessment: Matches the profile’s west-of-Ai summary and its caution that the modern ruin identification is not certain.

directNewReads.observedContentJa: The article is about ancient Bethel and gives a Joshua section focused on 7:2, 8:9, and 16:1; it does not establish the specific 12:16 king-list entry.
directNewReads.identityOrRelationAssessment: The profile’s Joshua 12:16 summary is grounded in the fixed biblical text; its Wikipedia note correctly says this article alone does not establish that particular correspondence or a precise modern site.

directNewReads.observedContentJa: The article describes Bezer as a Levitical/refuge city east of the Jordan and states that its site cannot be located with certainty.
directNewReads.identityOrRelationAssessment: Supports the profile’s refuge-city description and explicit unknown-site qualification.

directNewReads.observedContentJa: The redirect resolves to Kesalon (biblical); the page names Chesalon as an alternate form, cites Joshua 15:10, and links the place to the Judean Mountains, Kasla name preservation, and Iron Age remains.
directNewReads.identityOrRelationAssessment: Supports the biblical name and qualified modern association. It does not itself discuss translation differences in whether the phrase denotes a mountain or settlement; the profile’s note should not imply that this article establishes that distinction.

directNewReads.observedContentJa: The page redirects En-rogel to Ein Rogel, describes a spring near Jerusalem, says Bir Ayoub is the most common identification while some scholars dispute it, and covers the biblical boundary usage.
directNewReads.identityOrRelationAssessment: Matches the profile’s spring classification and its explicit uncertainty about Bir Ayoub/Silwan identification.

directNewReads.observedContentJa: The article identifies Gath-hepher as a border town, names Joshua 19:13, and says the ruin is near Mashhad, with Jonah tradition noted separately.
directNewReads.identityOrRelationAssessment: Supports the name and article’s proposed location; the profile correctly attributes the identification to Wikipedia and does not present this page as independent archaeological verification.

directNewReads.observedContentJa: The article is about the modern city and its history; it says ancient Israelite Hebron centered on Tel Rumeida and discusses the biblical conquest/Levite-city traditions, while the page carries an AI-content warning banner.
directNewReads.identityOrRelationAssessment: The profile’s article note limits the use to historical context and explicitly refuses to transfer the present city-centre coordinate to ancient Hebron. The AI-content warning further supports retaining this as contextual rather than primary geographic evidence.
